mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary inflation and tightening shock, which erodes real cash flows and raises risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistently low unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST remains above its 12-month moving average for six months.
